criterion.summary: p_astro > 0.5 (worded 'at least one half' and 'greater than one half'), following GWTC-3 and 4-OGC. Hanford-Livingston coincident BBH search only.
criterion.quote: We detect \neviasnew{} new BBH candidate events under the criterion that the astrophysical probability $\pastro$ is at least one half (which is also the threshold used in the GWTC-3 and 4-OGC catalogs).
criterion.section: Sec. I Introduction (macro \neviasnew = 6). Also: Abstract ('we continue to use an astrophysical probability of one half as our detection threshold, following the approach of the LVK catalogs'); Sec. V.B Concluding remarks ('based on the criteria that the astrophysical probability is greater than one half (following the LVK collaboration)'); Table I caption 'New events with $p_{\rm astro} > 0.5$'.

tiers.name: new events (6)
tiers.quote: We report the detection of \neviasnewtot{} new candidate binary black hole (BBH) merger signals in the publicly released data from the second half of the third observing run (O3b)

tiers.name: GWTC-3 HL BBH events re-detected (17)
tiers.quote: We confirm \neviasconf{} of these for a total of \neviastot{} detections in our analysis of the Hanford--Livingston coincident O3b data.

tiers.name: LVK events below threshold ('marginal'), vetoed or missed (not detections)
tiers.quote: we found that 6 of them were marginal in our catalog, i.e., recovered with a $\pastro$ lower than one half, while 6 were vetoed for failing one or more of our signal consistency and excess power tests, and one event was missed.

below_criterion.notes: All Table II rows failing p_astro > 0.5: GWTC-3 events vetoed (6), not recovered ('--': NSBH GW191219_163120 and missed GW200220_061928), below threshold (6 BBH plus NSBH GW200115_042309 at 0.12), and the 7 4-OGC-only (bold) events (5 below threshold, 2 vetoed). All names come from GWTC-3 or 4-OGC; this paper coins no name for a sub-threshold IAS candidate.

open_questions: IFAR convention: Sec. IV text says 'We compute the inverse false-alarm rate independently for each template bank', but the Table II IAS IFAR footnote says 'The combined IFAR across the chirp-mass banks'. Table I gives both.
Four of the six 'new' events (all except GW200225_075134 and GW191117_023843) are stated to be in the GWTC-3 sub-threshold candidate list; the paper still calls them new (paper_says_new=true).

Commented-out LaTeX (not in the rendered paper) holds an earlier draft's events GW191121_101441, GW191122_214924 (p_astro 0.51), GW191225_014544 (p_astro 0.85) and GW200323_135352; corner-plot files for GW191122_214924 remain in the tarball. Excluded; do not ingest them as IAS-O3b detections.

Same-day name collisions to keep apart: GW200210_100022 (new) vs GW200210_092254 (LVK, vetoed) vs GW200210_005122 (4-OGC, vetoed); GW200225_075134 vs GW200225_060421; GW200316_235947 vs GW200316_215756.
The '6 marginal' count covers BBH only; the NSBH GW200115_042309 also has IAS p_astro 0.12 in Table II.
Table II prints 4-OGC p_astro for GW200115_042309 as '-1.0' (source typo; irrelevant to IAS detection).
Counts check: Table I 6 rows; Table II 39 rows, 17 with IAS p_astro > 0.5, matching the paper's 17 confirmed and 23 total.
